assertions.name: u-leading-eps-coefficient-is-zero
assertions.source: u(1+ε) Taylor expansion ⇒ u is O(ε²), not a proper Taylor coord at q=1

assertions.name: v-leading-eps-coefficient-nonzero
assertions.source: v(1+ε) = sqrt(b)·ℏ leading coefficient ≠ 0 ⇒ v is O(ε), proper Taylor coord

assertions.name: w-leading-eps-coefficient
assertions.source: w(1+ε) = q-1/q leading coefficient = 2 ⇒ w is O(ε), proper Taylor coord

assertions.name: v-reconstruction-error-at-q-1p001
assertions.source: Σ c_k^(v) v^k truncated at order 6, reconstruct f(1.001)

assertions.name: w-reconstruction-error-at-q-1p001
assertions.source: Σ c_k^(w) w^k truncated at order 6, reconstruct f(1.001)

description: Pre-archimedean coordinate-choice probe: u vs v=√u vs w=q-1/q near q=1; Taylor comparison on reference f(q) = 4q/(q+1)².

structural_metrics.verdict_text: v strictly simpler at 3/7 orders. On this reference function, the eigenphase-argument coordinate v gives a simpler expansion than w. The c_k cross-anchor swing in u is likely a u-vs-v half-integer-packaging effect, not a Habiro-variable choice.
